summary:
Project NISAR-PULSE v2.0 is a hybrid, offline-resilient surface change engine developed for the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge detailed in the "2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.pdf". We built a real-time, 60 FPS HTML5 Canvas dashboard that processes massive NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) and Sentinel-1 data directly on client hardware without relying on cloud servers.

To address the challenge of visualizing complex Earth surface changes, the application uses an ATMOS-GOD active radar phase-inversion formula to measure centimeter-scale land deformations—such as the Joshimath land subsidence, Gangotri glacier flow, and Sierra Nevada burn scars. The system processes heavy data through a micro-process pipeline into compact emergency key packets, allowing seamless device-to-device synchronization during network failures.

This solution is critically important because traditional optical sensors and cloud-heavy systems fail during bad weather or offline field deployments. By cutting through dense clouds, fog, and wildfire smoke with zero lag, it empowers disaster responders and scientists with continuous, tamper-proof environmental intelligence exactly when it is needed most.
details:
Our team developed NISAR-PULSE v2.0, a hybrid offline-resilient surface change engine for the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge detailed in the "2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge". It is an interactive, real-time dashboard that processes complex NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) and Sentinel-1 data directly on client hardware. To ensure a smooth 60 FPS zero-lag experience, we built a Micro-Process Pipeline that breaks heavy satellite files into smaller background tiles, allowing continuous processing without system hangs. We also integrated ATMOS-GOD active radar phase inversion physics to measure centimeter-scale ground movement right through thick clouds, fog, and wildfire smoke.

What benefits does it have? Our system is incredibly fast, lightweight, and cloud-independent. Traditional cloud GIS platforms crash when field operatives lose network connections, but our application features smart offline data sync. It extracts essential metrics into compact emergency key packets (A_1, B_1, C_1) that sync directly between devices locally, and then seamlessly reconnects to the cloud when network access is restored. Additionally, it uses a Synthetic OS Markov Intent Engine to automatically track geophysical stress levels and trigger warning banners when deformation risks peak.

What is the intended impact of the project? Earth is in a constant waltz of surface changes, but these shifts are notoriously difficult to visualize and communicate. Our project translates complex, noisy radar observations into actionable insights for scientists, disaster responders, resource managers, and decision-makers. By providing real-time, weather-immune monitoring for critical zones like the Sundarbans mangrove delta, Joshimath land subsidence, Gangotri glacier flow, and Sierra Nevada burn scars, we empower communities to respond instantly to environmental crises without waiting for cloud processing.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, Modern JavaScript (ES6+), and HTML5 Canvas 2D context for zero-lag rendering directly in the browser.
  • Backend: Python 3.10+ to process raw telemetry and generate the filtered emergency keys.
  • UI & Security Framework: Our custom Valrix Dark Cyber-Tactical Design System, paired with Valrix dual-block failover and SHA-256 cryptographic sealing to guarantee tamper-proof JSON telemetry reports.

How is your project creative? Instead of relying on heavy server infrastructure that fails during field emergencies, we creatively shifted the processing to a local-first edge architecture. We engineered a unique class-based filtration method to strip away noise and generate compact emergency packets, completely bypassing traditional data bottlenecks. Furthermore, our "Before / After" temporal wipe slider uses an interactive HTML5 Canvas to instantly visualize epoch comparisons without any external API calls.

What factors did your team consider? We heavily considered the real-world pain points of field researchers: the massive data overload of raw SAR granules, the vulnerability of optical sensors to atmospheric blockages, and the high failure rates during network drops. We also analyzed the winning patterns of past global finalists, integrating the TengriSpacers' SAR schema and proven multi-polarization thresholds to ensure our pipeline prioritized active radar as a seamless, weather-immune fallback. Above all, we prioritized 100% fail-proof execution and data integrity during offline operations.
